'''Madhab Chandra Dash''' (born 1939 in Puri, Odisha) is an Indian ecologist and environmental biologist. He is currently a member of the Appellate Authority, Water (PCP) Act, 1974 Government of Orissa.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority">{{cite web |url=http://orienvappellateauthority.nic.in/MC-Dash.html |title=Bio-data of Prof. (Dr.) Madhab Chandra Dash |publisher=Appellate Authority |accessdate=2012-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140725141432/http://orienvappellateauthority.nic.in/MC-Dash.html |archive-date=25 July 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="nieindia">http://www.nieindia.org/ijees/PDF/V34/34-223.pdf{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He is a former vice chancellor of [[Sambalpur University]] (2001–2004).<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" /> He is a past chairman of the Orissa State Pollution Control Board (1997–2001) and a former member of the Central Pollution Control Board, New Delhi.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" /><ref name="nieindia" /><ref name="orissahighcourt">{{cite web|url=http://orissahighcourt.nic.in/courtnews/IssueNo-XII.pdf |title=News Bulletin April–July 08 |accessdate=2012-10-20}}</ref>

Dash taught ecology at the School of Life Sciences, in Sambalpur University from 1973 until 1997 and was instrumental in expansion of the department as well as making it one of the early academic departments in India to focus on a broader life science curricula. He became a full professor in 1975 and was the head of the department from 1974 until 1987.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" />

==Educational background==
Madhab Chandra Dash was born in 1939 in [[Puri (city)|Puri]], [[Orissa, India|Orissa]] in a [[Utkala Brahmin|Brahmin]] family.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Mishra |first=P. C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iPEegmF3IB4C&dq=madhab+chandra+dash+brahmin&pg=PR15 |title=Advances in Ecology and Environmental Sciences |date=1995 |publisher=APH Publishing |isbn=978-81-7024-676-3 |language=en}}</ref> He completed an undergraduate degree in Zoology (Honours) from [[Ravenshaw College]] in Cuttack and later completed a masters in Zoology at [[Utkal University]].<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" /> Dash received his doctoral (PhD) degree in 1970 from the [[University of Calgary]] under the guidance of J. B. Cragg.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" /><ref name="archivescanada">{{cite web |url=http://www.archivescanada.ca/english/search/ItemDisplay.asp?sessionKey=999999999_142&l=0&lvl=1&v=0&coll=1&itm=252218&rt=1&bill=1 |title=Archives Canada |accessdate=2012-10-14 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130419025627/http://www.archivescanada.ca/english/search/ItemDisplay.asp?sessionKey=999999999_142&l=0&lvl=1&v=0&coll=1&itm=252218&rt=1&bill=1# |archive-date=2013-04-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="dspace.ucalgary">{{cite journal|url=https://dspace.ucalgary.ca/handle/1880/15034 |title=Ecology of enchytraeidae (Oligochaeta) in Rocky Mountain forest soils (Kananaskis region, Alberta, Canada) |year=1970 |publisher=DSpace at University of Calgary |doi=10.11575/PRISM/17296 |accessdate=2012-10-14|last1=Dash |first1=Madhab Chandra }}</ref> His thesis was titled "Ecology of enchytraeidae (Oligochaeta) in Rocky Mountain forest soils (Kananaskis region, Alberta, Canada)".<ref name="Dash1970">{{cite book|author=M C. Dash|title=Ecology of enchytraeidae (Oligochaeta) in Rocky Mountain forest soils (Kananaskis region, Alberta, Canada|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ScXKZwEACAAJ|accessdate=20 October 2012|year=1970|publisher=University of Calgary}}</ref>

After completing his PhD, he returned to India and help grow biological sciences in the State of Orissa and joined the School of Life Sciences at Sambalpur University.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" />

==Contributions==
Dash has done pioneering work in vermitechnology, soil ecology, conservation of sea turtles, population biology, quantitative ecology, energetics of soil oligochaetes, larval energetics of amphibia, environmental impact assessment (EIA), sustainable development, environmental pollution and its mitigation. He has been instrumental in providing guidance to 41 doctoral students and numerous masters students.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" /><ref name="Mishra1995">{{cite book|author=Pramod Chandra Mishra|title=Advances In Ecology And Environmental Sciences|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iPEegmF3IB4C&pg=PR6|accessdate=20 October 2012|date=1 January 1995|publisher=APH Publishing|isbn=978-81-7024-676-3|pages=xv–xxiii}}</ref>

His work on vermitechnology was one of the earliest in India during the late 1970s<ref name="nieindia_a">http://www.nieindia.org/ijees/PDF/35-163.pdf{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and he produced one of the early studies on turtle migration and breeding on the coast of Orissa (Gahirmatha).<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" /><ref name="trove">{{cite web|url=http://trove.nla.gov.au/work/20891067?selectedversion=NBD8343477 |title=The turtle paradise, Gahirmatha : an ecological analysis and conservation strategy |author=Madhab Chandra Dash |author2=Chandra Sekhar Kar |publisher=Trove |accessdate=2012-10-14}}</ref> He co-authored one of the earliest book on turtle migrations and population studies to the east coast of India, Gahirmatha in Orissa in 1990.<ref name="trove" /> He has conducted work on environmental pollution especially in relation to iron-ore industries, steel and aluminium industries.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" />

Dash was a former Member, National Expert Committee for EIA & EMP of Mining Projects (1995–1997 – 3 years), of the Ministry of Environment & Forests, Government of India, New Delhi.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" />

From 2002 until 2005, he was the Chairman of the National Steering Committee (which consisted of ten high level expert members) for Tropical Soil Biology and Fertility programmes sponsored by TSBF, Nairobi, UNEP, MoEF, (Govt. of India), [[Jawaharlal Nehru University]], New Delhi on "Conservation and Sustainable Management for Below Ground Bio-diversity" operating at multiple centers and also contributed to the second phase of the programme from 2007 until 2009.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" />

Dash was the Chairman, Expert Committee (that consisted of 11 members) for Environmental clearance to the Thermal Power Plants set up by Ministry of Environment and Forests (MoEF notification No. S.O.-319(E)) from April, 1997 to 2008 by Government of Orissa, Bhubaneswar.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" />

He was the Chairman of the visiting team of [[National Assessment and Accreditation Council]] (UGC), Bangalore to Colleges and Universities – from 2002 to 2007. He has led over 15 major research projects in Ecology and Environmental Sciences, EIA & EMP etc. sponsored by variety of national and international institutions such as Smithsonian, USA, World Bank, UGC & CSIR, New Delhi, MoEF, New Delhi, Govt. of Orissa.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" /><ref name="www-wds.worldbank">{{cite web|url=http://www-wds.worldbank.org/external/default/WDSContentServer/WDSP/IB/2008/02/12/000333038_20080212024858/Rendered/PDF/E18000EA0P09341SAR1EA1P0934780Vol.1.pdf |title=World Bank Document |accessdate=2012-10-14}}</ref>

Dash has been an expert advisor to the "House Committee on Environment" of Orissa Legislative Assembly, Government of Orissa since 2005.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" /> Prof. Dash has also consulted widely by the industry especially on environment matters (EIA, EMP, Environmental Law).<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" />

Dash has published more than 200 peer reviewed scientific papers and authored more than 17 books and numerous book chapters for leading publishers across the world such as Cambridge University Press UK, Academic Press USA, Macmillan India and Tata McGraw Hill, India.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" /><ref name="tatamcgrawhill">{{cite book|url=http://www.tatamcgrawhill.com/html/9780070083660.html |title=FUNDAMENTALS OF ECOLOGY |author=M. Dash |author2=S. Dash |year=2009 |publisher=Tata – McGraw-Hill Education |isbn=9780070083660 |accessdate=2012-10-14}}</ref><ref name="highered.mcgraw-hill">{{cite web|url=http://highered.mcgraw-hill.com/sites/dl/free/0070083665/802001/About_the_Authors.pdf |title=Bio highered.mcgraw-hill.com }}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
Dash was awarded by the State Government of the Orissa in 1991 its highest scientific honour (Samanta Chandrasekhar Award) for his seminal contributions of life sciences research.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" />

He is a fellow of Fellow, National Academy of Science (Allahabad), India and a Fellow, National Institute of Ecology (New Delhi), India.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" />

Two species of Indian earthworms have been named after him for his contribution to the field of vermitechnology.<ref name="orienvappellateauthority" />
